description: Adversaries may attempt to exploit SQL injection vulnerabilities in Internet-facing web applications to gain unauthorized access to backend databases. By injecting malicious SQL code into input fields, query parameters, or HTTP headers, attackers can bypass authentication, extract sensitive data, modify or delete database records, and in some cases achieve remote code execution on the underlying server.

patterns.description: Characteristics within HTTP requests that indicate SQL injection attempts targeting web application input vectors.

features.name: Malicious SQL Syntax in Payloads
features.description: HTTP request parameters, form fields, or headers contain recognizable SQL keywords and operators such as 'UNION SELECT', 'OR 1=1', 'DROP TABLE', single quotes, comment sequences ('--', '/*'), and CHAR() encoding used to manipulate backend database queries.

features.name: Encoded and Obfuscated Payloads
features.description: Attackers frequently use URL encoding (%27 for single quote), double encoding, hex encoding (0x), or CHAR() functions to evade Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) and input validation filters while still delivering executable SQL to the backend.

patterns.description: Anomalies in the request patterns indicating automated SQL injection scanning or exploitation.

features.name: Rapid Sequential Requests to Same Endpoint
features.description: A high volume of HTTP requests (High Flow Pkts/s) directed at the same URL endpoint or form, each with slightly different parameter values as the attacker iterates through injection payloads using automated tools like sqlmap.

features.name: Asymmetric Response Sizes (Data Exfiltration)
features.description: Successful SQL injection often causes the server to return abnormally large responses (High Bwd Packet Length Mean) containing extracted database contents, compared to the small malicious request sent by the attacker (Low Fwd Packet Length Mean).

patterns.description: Timing behaviors associated with different SQL injection techniques.

features.name: Time-Based Blind SQLi Delays
features.description: In blind SQL injection attacks, the attacker uses time-delay functions (SLEEP(), WAITFOR DELAY, BENCHMARK()) causing artificially prolonged server response times (High Flow Duration, High Flow IAT Mean) as the database pauses execution to confirm true/false conditions.

features.name: Machine-Speed Request Pacing
features.description: Automated SQL injection tools send requests at machine speed (Low Flow IAT Mean between requests) with minimal or zero inter-arrival times, far faster than any human user could submit form data.

patterns.description: Contextual indicators for distinguishing SQL injection attacks from legitimate application traffic.

features.name: Error-Based Reconnaissance
features.description: Initial probing often triggers HTTP 500 Internal Server Errors or verbose database error messages (MySQL, MSSQL, Oracle syntax errors) in the server responses, revealing the backend database type and structure to the attacker.

features.name: Legitimate Complex Queries (False Positive Filtering)
features.description: Some legitimate web applications, particularly search engines, analytics dashboards, or reporting tools, may naturally generate complex parameterized queries that superficially resemble SQL injection patterns in network traffic analysis.
